title: Using HLRS Hazel Hen Supercomputer
author: Theresa Pollinger
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ud8es9w

steps.title: Request Hazel Hen Access
steps.instruction: Request access to the Hazel Hen supercomputer using your project ID via the HLRS academic users portal.

substeps.instruction: Submit the request form as a real paper.
Ensure project administrators submit your username, password, and IP addresses.

steps.title: Access Supercomputer and Create Workspace
steps.instruction: Log into the system and establish a working environment.

substeps.instruction: Connect via SSH using the command: ssh ipvuser@hazelhen.hww.de (replace ipvuser with your username).
Create a workspace using the command: ws_allocate myWorkspace 60, or navigate to an existing group workspace located under /lustre/cray/ws8/ws/

steps.title: Configure SSH Keys for Git
steps.instruction: Generate and distribute SSH keys on Hazel Hen to enable repository cloning.

substeps.instruction: Generate a new SSH key using ssh-keygen.
Copy the public key (output of cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub) to the required GitHub or GitLab accounts.

steps.title: Clone Repositories via Reverse SSH Tunnel
steps.instruction: From your local computer (on the approved IP list), use a reverse SSH tunnel to clone repositories onto the supercomputer.

substeps.instruction: Execute the tunnel and clone command: ssh -R 7890:simsgs.informatik.uni-stuttgart.de:22 ipvuser@hazelhen.hww.de git clone ssh://git@localhost:7890/heenemo/combi.git /lustre/cray/ws8/ws/ipvuser-myWorkspace/combi
Note: Replace '7890' with a different port for every git remote server used.

steps.title: Configure Environment and Build Tools
steps.instruction: Set up the necessary software modules and environment variables for building code.

substeps.instruction: Enter the workspace on Hazel Hen and check out the required code versions.
Load required modules (e.g., gnu compiler suite: module load PrgEnv-gnu).
Use 'module avail' to check available modules; install missing tools locally or request them via the CRAY XC40 local Modules wiki.
Set the environment variable for dynamic linking: export CRAYPE_LINK_TYPE=dynamic
Document the configuration using 'module list' and 'declare -p', and push code changes via git.

steps.title: Execute Jobs on MOM Nodes
steps.instruction: Request and run jobs on the compute nodes.

substeps.instruction: Request an interactive job on a MOM node using: qsub -I -l nodes=1:ppn=24,walltime=01:00:00
Submit jobs via aprun (not mpirun) using a bash script containing: #PBS -N, #PBS -l nodes=:ppn=24, #PBS -l walltime=00:01:00, cd $PBS_O_WORKDIR, and export OMP_NUM_THREADS=
